RECOMMENDATION: DON'T RAISE IT
LIKELIHOOD: 0

Both you and the successful candidate are men. An all-male panel selecting one man over another does not suggest sex discrimination against you, as you both share the same sex. While an all-male panel may reflect broader diversity issues within the firm's leadership, it provides no evidence of sex bias in choosing between two male applicants.

Raising sex discrimination would undermine your credibility and distract from legitimate inquiries. The hiring decision appears driven by other factors—such as the selected candidate's client relationships, interview performance, or potentially age. Instead, follow up professionally on your request for constructive feedback regarding qualifications and role competencies.
